sections.content:
Ready to learn **Character Data Type and Operations**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Working with char type
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **Character Data Type and Operations** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
char letter = 'A';
char digit = '9';
char unicode = '\u0041';  // 'A'

System.out.println((int) letter);   // 65 (ASCII value)
System.out.println(Character.isLetter(letter));   // true
System.out.println(Character.isDigit(digit));     // true
System.out.println(Character.toUpperCase('a'));   // 'A'

sections.title: Key Points
points: A char stores a single 16-bit Unicode character (e.g., 'A', '9', '\u0041')
Characters have numeric values: 'A' is 65, 'a' is 97, '0' is 48 in ASCII/Unicode
Character.isLetter(), isDigit(), toUpperCase(), toLowerCase() are useful utility methods
Casting between char and int converts between the character and its Unicode value
Comparing characters compares their Unicode values: 'a' < 'b' is true

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Character Data Type and Operations - Working with char type. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.
